mathematical_justification.clause: Full local triple domain and actual ordered positions
mathematical_justification.assessment: IncreasingBoundaryTriple consists of any three Fin n positions lower<middle<upper. The hypothesis compares H1 and H2 for every such triple with J.left<=lower and upper<=J.right; the middle is automatically between the endpoints. liftTriple translates each of the three positions by J.left. globalPosition_bounds proves these actual translated endpoints lie in J, so the hypothesis applies to every local triple. Function extensionality then gives equality of the entire restricted arrays. No entries outside J are constrained, and no geometry, determinant or sign-valued restriction is imposed on the arbitrary ring arrays.

farOnlyCoordinates is the actual constructed inverse nearFarInverse(0,H)(E), not a free solution variable. Equality of the restricted H arrays therefore gives equality of their constructed local c arrays by congruence. The proved farOnlyCoordinates_restrict identifies each with the restriction of the corresponding global c. For J.leaves>=2, the full local interval has at least three vertices and lifts exactly to J. Evaluating the array equalities at this full interval and composing both restriction equations yields c1(J)=c2(J). This is a source-faithful derivation from the established exact restriction theorem instead of repeating source interval-length induction; it assumes neither the locality conclusion nor an additional inverse-uniqueness premise.

Every BoundaryInterval has positive leaf count. The proof separately handles J.leaves=1 using the proved identity c(H)(J)=1 for every H, so it never invokes a two-vertex polygon coefficient or a nonexistent geometric G1 condition. If leaves is not one, positivity yields leaves>=2. An independent leaf consumer verifies equality with no array-agreement hypothesis. Two further consumers show equality of the entire restricted c array and of its value on every actual translated local subinterval; this checks that the coordinate locality is compatible with all source subintervals, not only one abstract target.

The critical triple is an actual IncreasingBoundaryTriple with pairwise distinct ordered positions x<y<z. The hypothesis allows only that one array entry to differ; it does not require a sign flip or assume geometry. If J does not contain both x and z, any triple whose endpoints lie inside J cannot equal critical: otherwise its bounds would contradict the stated exclusion. Applying the local theorem therefore gives unchanged c. The inclusive inequalities are exact containment of I*=[x,z]; a proper subinterval or a gap may meet its endpoints and is still excluded unless it contains the full span. There is no requirement that J be disjoint from the critical points.

The left gap is the actual interval [critical.lower,critical.middle]. Containing the full critical span would require critical.upper<=critical.middle, contradicting strict ordering. The right gap similarly would require critical.middle<=critical.lower. Independent consumers verify unchanged c on both, including singleton gaps. For every raw nonunary composition of the exact critical span, the existing strict child-leaf-count theorem gives each child fewer leaves than the span. If a child contained the span, the endpoint inequalities would force its leaf count to be at least that of the span, a contradiction. Thus every actual proper child has unchanged c, as needed in the next source paragraph285; no subset of compositions or child indices is assumed.

mathematical_justification.clause: Scope is a partial algebraic source proof step
mathematical_justification.assessment: The theorem starts at source229, its proof at270, and the locality paragraph is281-283. The first sentence of that paragraph additionally says that the critical triple appears as far data in exactly one coordinate formula. These three helper declarations do not themselves formalize that occurrence statement, nor do they derive equality of all noncritical geometric arrays from a continuous wall germ after a common shrink. They do not prove gap G1, epsilon signs, contracted polygons, composition splitting, coefficient jumps or propagation through larger intervals. Their conditional algebraic locality conclusion is faithful and useful, but the full thm:single-triple remains unaccepted.
